body:
Reviewed exact HEAD `09d76114cb64be0a7764a3fa3ee49cee0c63e19a` against `develop@11c3b57`.

The ordered B → C−B producer repairs the prior class/module fixture and order issue. The bounded Schema self-check reuse and preserved quality floors are also appropriate. One reproducible selector regression still blocks acceptance; this is not a request to broaden the optimization or add another testing system.

**[P1] Function-local imports must shadow a module-level fixed path binding.** The new lexical binding table records `ast.Name(Store)` but not names introduced by `Import` / `ImportFrom`. A function-local `from project_config import ROOT` therefore resolves to the unrelated module-level `ROOT` during path inference.

Minimal consumer:
```python
from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
def test_document():
    from project_config import ROOT  # project_config.ROOT = Path("docs")
    assert (ROOT / "input.md").read_text() == "good"
```
For a change to `docs/input.md`, the actual test fails when the contents change from `good` to `bad`. With the same complete synthetic snapshot, accepted `11c3b57` selects `test_reader`, while `09d7611` returns `selected={}`, excludes `test_reader`, and reports no analysis error. I independently reran this counterexample.

Please account for import-bound names in the applicable lexical scope. An imported root that cannot be resolved should retain the existing unknown-reader dependency boundary instead of falling through to an outer fixed root. Cover the local import shadowing case (including aliased imports where applicable) in the existing dependency regressions. Keep the ordered producer, successful Schema self-check cache, thresholds and other accepted improvements.

After this narrow repair, satisfy the existing checks for a selector change on the final commit; no additional full-test policy, sandbox or performance threshold is requested. PR70 is not merged in this review.
